subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Vehicle-to-Grid Technology
description: A quick win: understand Vehicle-to-Grid Technology.

hook.text: Your parked EV has a giant battery sitting idle. What if it could power your house—or the grid?

buildup.text: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) lets EVs send electricity back when demand is high and prices spike.

discovery.text: A single EV battery holds enough energy to power an average home for two to three days.

twist.text: During blackouts, bidirectional EVs can act as backup generators—the Ford F-150 Lightning already does this.

climax.text: If millions of EVs feed the grid during peak hours, it could reduce the need for new power plants.

punchline.text: Parked EVs could become the world's largest battery.

quiz.question: What does vehicle-to-grid allow EVs to do?
options: Send electricity back to the grid

details.summary: Vehicle-to-grid technology allows parked EVs to feed stored electricity back into the power grid during peak demand, turning millions of car batteries into a distributed energy storage network.
details.whyItMatters: V2G could solve renewable energy's intermittency problem. A fleet of EV batteries storing surplus solar and wind energy and releasing it at peak demand would reduce the need for fossil fuel peaker plants.
takeaways: EVs can send stored electricity back to the grid when demand peaks
Millions of EV batteries could form a massive distributed energy reserve
V2G requires bidirectional chargers and utility cooperation

faq.question: Would V2G degrade my car's battery faster?
faq.answer: Additional charge cycles do cause some extra wear. However, smart V2G systems limit discharge depth and frequency to minimize degradation. Some studies suggest grid services income could offset any additional battery wear costs.

faq.question: How much could EV owners earn from V2G?
faq.answer: Estimates range from $50 to $200 per month depending on electricity prices and grid demand. Pilot programs in the UK and Netherlands are testing real earnings. The financial incentive could significantly reduce EV ownership costs.
